outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has acquired one claimed unconditional proof of its infinitude part (OpenAI, preprint path-dated 4 October 2026, public in the openai/math repository from 6 October 2026, produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, unrefereed, and disputed as to whether it is unconditional), one unrefereed human arXiv claim whose general-base version dates from 2018 and whose asymptotic version first appears in February 2026, one conditional human claim (Murty and Naik, August 2026), and several GRH-conditional or partial results; I found no refereed proof of the bullet as stated.
problem_asks: Single claim, universally quantified. (1) For every integer a that is neither a perfect square nor -1: (2) a is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes p. The bullet asks only for infinitude. It does not state the predicted density (Artin's constant or a rational multiple), which appears in the Wikipedia lead but not in the bullet's statement. A proof of infinitude addresses all of the bullet; a density result would address more than the bullet asks.

events.what_happened: C. Hooley, 'On Artin's conjecture', J. reine angew. Math. 225 (1967) 209-220. Proves the conjecture (with the Lehmers' density correction) conditional on GRH for certain Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer extensions. Known from the raw Wikipedia reference list and secondary summaries; the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH for the Kummer-field zeta functions: every admissible a is a primitive root for a positive-density set of primes, so infinitude follows under that hypothesis.
events.remains: Unconditional infinitude for every admissible a.

checked_by.who: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (vol. 225, 1967, pp. 209-220), per the DOI in the Wikipedia reference list; not opened

events.direction: Conditional proof of the infinitude claim; cuts in the direction the conjecture points, under GRH.

events.what_happened: R. Gupta and M. Ram Murty, unconditional partial result, dated 1983 or 1984 (sources differ; one gives Inventiones vol. 78, 1984). A specific set of 13 bases is shown such that at least one of them is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. Later reduced to 7 by Gupta, Murty and Murty and to 3 by Heath-Brown. Known from search-result summaries and the Wikipedia text; not opened.
events.delivers: Unconditional: at least one of 13 specified integers is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. Says nothing about any given a.
events.remains: Infinitude for each individual a, including a = 2.
events.direction: Partial unconditional result; does not decide any specific a, so it cuts neither way on the bullet as stated.

events.what_happened: Stephens (1969): unconditional asymptotic for N_a(x) for almost all a in a range about exp(6 (log x log log x)^{1/2}). Known only as cited in the Klurman-Shparlinski-Teravainen abstract page and an MPIM seminar summary; not opened.
events.delivers: Asymptotic for almost all a in a short range; not for any specific a.
events.remains: Every individual a.
events.direction: Average-over-a result toward the predicted asymptotic; cuts neither way on any specific a.

events.what_happened: D. R. Heath-Brown, 'Artin's conjecture for primitive roots', Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) 37 (1986) 27-38. Unconditional: at most two integers a fail the conjecture; at least one of 2, 3, 5 is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes (Corollary 1). Wikipedia also records at most three square-free exceptions and at most c(ln x)^2 exceptions up to x. Known from the Wikipedia text and search summaries; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Unconditional, for all but at most two integers a: infinitude of primes with a as primitive root. Also: at least one of the three integers 2, 3, 5 works infinitely often. The three are not identified, and a = 2 is not known to work.
events.remains: Infinitude for each of the at most two exceptional a, and for each of 2, 3, 5 individually.

checked_by.who: Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (Oxford), refereed journal
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (vol. 37, 1986, pp. 27-38), per the DOI in the Wikipedia reference list; not opened

events.direction: Partial unconditional result toward infinitude; cuts in the direction the conjecture points for all but two a, and for the three named integers collectively.

events.what_happened: C. Virdol, Kyoto J. Math.: 2016, infinite part of Artin's conjecture for general abelian varieties; 2020, strong form for general CM elliptic curves. Known from the Wikipedia text (fetched through a summarising model); not opened and the exact dates were not verified beyond the years.
events.delivers: Analogues for abelian varieties and CM elliptic curves, not for the integers.
events.remains: The bullet, for integers a.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the two papers per the Wikipedia text; not opened
checked_by.where: not located; cited in the Wikipedia article (fetched)

events.direction: Analogue; cuts toward the conjecture's analogue, not the integer case.

events.what_happened: L. Hochfilzer and E. Waxman, 'On Artin's Primitive Root Conjecture for Function Fields over F_q', arXiv:2306.04297 (v1 7 Jun 2023; v2 13 Jul 2023, comment 'minor revisions'). Abstract claims to complete the proof of the conjecture for function fields over F_q, generalising to function fields in r variables and dropping the geometric assumption on g, via an exponential-sum estimate from Weil's theorem. The abstract states no extra hypothesis. Abstract page opened; body not read.
events.delivers: Unconditional, per the abstract, for function fields over F_q. A different setting: says nothing about the integers.
events.remains: The bullet, for the integers, entirely.
events.doubts: Peer status not confirmed in my searches. The result is an analogue in a different setting, so it does not bear on the integers' scope.
events.direction: Analogue; the function-field version is claimed in the direction the conjecture points. Cuts neither way on the integers.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, arXiv:1707.06517, v1 (14 Jul 2017), titled 'Densities For The Repeating Decimals Problems'. Abstract, for base 10 only: the counting function pi_10(x) = #{p <= x : ord_p(10) = p-1} is at least a constant times x/log x for all large x. No conditional hypothesis is stated. The same base-10 content is in v3 (20 Sep 2017), v5 (21 Apr 2018) and v7 (6 Oct 2018), all checked; v2, v4 and v6 were not checked. The general-u version first appears at v8 (next event).
events.revisions: v1 14 Jul 2017 (base 10); v2 14 Aug 2017 (not checked); v3 20 Sep 2017 (base 10); v4 21 Oct 2017 (not checked); v5 21 Apr 2018 (base 10); v6 8 Sep 2018 (not checked); v7 6 Oct 2018 (base 10); superseded by the general-u version at v8, 17 Nov 2018.
events.delivers: If correct: infinitude (indeed x/log x growth) of primes p for which 10 is a primitive root. This settles the bullet for the single integer a = 10 only.
events.remains: Every other admissible a.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 years (to 11 Oct 2026); no review, journal decision or citation found in my searches
events.doubts: The base-10 claim is a special case of the general claim from v8 onward, and the abstract gives no argument. The later general claim (next event) carries the same unreviewed status.
events.direction: Would settle one case (a = 10) in the direction the bullet points.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, 'Primitive Root Conjecture in Arithmetic Progressions', arXiv:1701.03188 (v1 11 Jan 2017; v7 28 Sep 2025). Abstract, read from the abs page (body not read): for a fixed integer u (u not +-1 or v^2) and primes p = qn + a with q = O(log^c x), an asymptotic count with main term delta(u,q,a) x/log x and error O(x/log^b x), b = b(c) > 1. The abstract does not mention GRH.
events.revisions: v1 11 Jan 2017; v2 26 Sep 2017; v3 21 Oct 2017; v4 19 Sep 2018; v5 6 Oct 2018; v6 15 Sep 2021; v7 28 Sep 2025 (current in my fetch). Only v1 and v7 abstracts were read directly.
events.delivers: As stated, asymptotic for primes in progressions of bounded-or-logarithmic modulus. Read literally with q = 1 (within q = O(log^c x)), it would contain the bullet's claim, but the abstract does not state the q = 1 case.
events.remains: The abstract does not say what it gives with q = 1; if it does not include that case, the bullet is not addressed.
events.doubts: Its scope may include the bullet's claim, but the abstract does not say so. The body was not read, so whether the progression result is unconditional, and whether the q = 1 case holds, is unknown.
events.direction: If its range is read to include q = 1, it cuts in the direction of infinitude; the abstract does not state this.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, arXiv:1707.06517, v8 (17 Nov 2018), retitled 'Densities Of Primes And Primitive Roots'. Abstract: 'Let u != +-1, v^2 be a fixed integer ... This note provides an effective lower bound pi_u(x) = #{p <= x : ord_p(u) = p-1} >> x (log x)^{-1} ... for all large numbers x', with no conditional hypothesis stated. It says that current literature gives >> x (log x)^{-2} and only for restricted sets of at least three integers. The same lower-bound claim is in v9 (20 Aug 2025), v10 (30 Aug 2025), v12 (8 Oct 2025) and v13 (15 Nov 2025) (abstract pages checked; v11, 28 Sep 2025, not checked). Body not read.
events.revisions: v8 17 Nov 2018 (first general-u claim); v9 20 Aug 2025 (same lower-bound claim, 'Densities Of Primes And Primitive Roots'); v10 30 Aug 2025 (same); v11 28 Sep 2025 (not checked); v12 8 Oct 2025 (same, 'Refined analysis of the error term'); v13 15 Nov 2025 (same); v14 14 Feb 2026 (asymptotic claim; next event).
events.delivers: If correct: for each admissible u (u != +-1, v^2 is exactly the bullet's class), infinitude of primes with u as primitive root, via pi_u(x) >> x/log x for all large x. This is the whole bullet.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet, if correct. The density is not asked by the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 years 11 months to 11 Oct 2026 (v8); no review, journal publication or citing work found in my searches
events.doubts: (a) The claimed bound is stronger than the literature the abstract itself cites (x/log^2 x, and only for restricted sets of at least three integers), and it reaches every admissible u. Hooley's 1967 argument needs GRH for the Kummer-field zeta functions, and a 2026 blog (Persiflage, 8 Oct 2026, replying to a commenter) says that Hooley's argument 'needs full GRH for these'. Nothing I found explains how the 2018 note avoids that step. (b) The base-10 versions before it (v1-v7) had different titles and content, so the general claim is first visible at v8. (c) The Wikipedia article's reference list (as fetched; ten references) does not include this paper, and no citing work was found; the 2025 Fan-Pollack abstract describes the conjecture as unsolved since 1927 and the 2026 Murty-Naik abstract does not cite it in the abstract (bibliography not fully checked).
events.direction: If correct, proves infinitude for every admissible u, cutting in the direction the conjecture points, with no counterexample.

events.what_happened: A. Perucca and I. E. Shparlinski, 'Uniform bounds for the density in Artin's conjecture on primitive roots', arXiv:2401.11589 (one version, 21 Jan 2024). Under GRH, for an element alpha of a number field K, bounds the ratio between the Artin density and the Artin constant A(tau), assuming the density is nonzero. Over Q the ratio lies in [2/3, 2]. Abstract page opened.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH and assuming a nonzero density: a two-sided bound on the density relative to A(tau), for number fields, with the rational case in [2/3, 2]. Says nothing about infinitude for the integers.
events.remains: The bullet, for every integer a (the density bound is a quantitative refinement, not infinitude).
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 9 months; engagement not searched specifically
events.direction: Quantitative refinement under GRH of the density form of the conjecture; cuts toward the conjecture conditionally, with no counterexample.

events.what_happened: N. Kimmel, 'Artin's Primitive Root Conjecture in Number Fields and For Matrices', arXiv:2306.15973 (v1 28 Jun 2023; v2 9 Aug 2023; v3 21 Nov 2024). Variants for number fields and matrices; the abstract says 'All results are conditional on GRH'. Extends Roskam's quadratic-extension results to higher-degree extensions. Published in Acta Arithmetica 216 (2024) per a search summary (journal page not opened). Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v1 28 Jun 2023; v2 9 Aug 2023; v3 21 Nov 2024 (current in my fetch).
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH: order of an element of a number field modulo rational primes, and of a matrix over Q modulo primes, almost-maximal for almost all p under Galois-group constraints. An analogue, not the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet for the integers, entirely.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (vol. 216, 2024, online Nov 2024) per a search summary; journal page not opened

events.direction: Conditional analogue; cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: S. Naik, 'Matsuda monoids and Artin's primitive root conjecture', arXiv:2410.09694 (one version, 13 Oct 2024). For the additive monoid generated by 2 and 3, establishes unconditionally (Daileda had shown it under GRH) that it is not a Matsuda monoid of type l for any prime l, 'using its connection with Artin's primitive root conjecture'. Abstract page opened; body not read.
events.delivers: Unconditional settlement of a Matsuda-monoid question for the monoid generated by 2 and 3. It does not assert Artin's conjecture for any a. The abstract does not say which Artin-type input it uses.
events.remains: All of the bullet. The result is about a different question.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years; engagement not searched specifically
events.direction: Different question; cuts neither way on the bullet as far as the abstract states.

events.what_happened: O. Klurman, I. E. Shparlinski and J. Teraväinen, 'On Artin's conjecture on average and short character sums', arXiv:2412.13355 (v1 17 Dec 2024; v2 23 Jan 2026). Shows that N_a(x), the number of primes up to x for which a is a primitive root, satisfies the Artin-predicted asymptotic for almost all 1 <= a <= exp((log log x)^2). Improves Stephens (1969); uses a new short character sum estimate extending Garaev (2006). Published Bull. London Math. Soc. 57 (2025), 2429-2443 (DOI 10.1112/blms.70103, from search results). Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v1 17 Dec 2024; v2 23 Jan 2026 (comment: '15 pages; referee comments incorporated'). BLMS vol. 57, issue 8, 2025, early online 23 May 2025 (per search results).
events.delivers: Asymptotic for N_a(x) for almost all a in a range growing with x. The statement is an average over a: its exceptional set is controlled only in density, so it does not establish the property for any specific a, including 2.
events.remains: Infinitude for each individual a, including the at most two exceptions and 2, 3, 5 individually.

events.what_happened: S. G. Hazra, M. Ram Murty and J. Sivaraman, 'A note on the two variable Artin's conjecture', J. Number Theory 262 (2024) 161-185. Improves the unconditional lower bound for the two-variable Artin set (primes p for which a mod p lies in the subgroup generated by b mod p), for any three multiplicatively independent integers. Online 23 Apr 2024 (journal); arXiv posting not checked. Known from a search summary; not opened.
events.revisions: Received 19 Sep 2023; revised 1 Mar 2024; accepted 1 Mar 2024; online 23 Apr 2024 (per search summary).
events.delivers: Unconditional lower bound for a two-variable analogue, for three multiplicatively independent integers. An analogue, not the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet, entirely.
events.doubts: The date is the journal's online date. If an arXiv posting before 26 Jan 2024 exists, the event would predate the window; not checked.
events.direction: Analogue; cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: L. Goldmakher, G. Martin and P. Péringuey, 'Refinements of Artin's primitive root conjecture', arXiv:2502.19601 (one version, 26 Feb 2025). Proposes several conjectures on finer properties of the order of a modulo p, of which Artin's conjecture is a special case. Proves them under GRH, and proves weaker versions unconditionally; the abstract does not specify those weaker statements. Abstract page opened; body not read.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH: refinements that contain Artin's conjecture as a special case. Unconditional weaker versions, which the abstract does not state.
events.remains: Artin's conjecture itself, for every a, unconditionally.
events.time_since_posted: about 7.5 months; engagement not searched specifically
events.doubts: The unconditional weaker versions are not described in the abstract, so their bearing on the bullet is unknown. Not checked in the body.
events.direction: Conditional refinements; cuts toward the conjecture only under GRH, plus unspecified weaker unconditional statements.

events.what_happened: K. (Steve) Fan and P. Pollack, 'Counting primes with a given primitive root, uniformly', arXiv:2505.05601 (v1 8 May 2025; v2 14 Sep 2025). Under GRH, a uniform Artin-Hooley asymptotic whenever log x / log log 2|g| tends to infinity; under GRH, the least prime with g as a primitive root is O(log^19(2|g|)) for all non-square g != -1. Abstract page opened.
events.revisions: v1 8 May 2025; v2 14 Sep 2025 (current in my fetch).
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH: uniform asymptotic for the count of primes with g as a primitive root, and a least-prime bound. Under GRH this includes infinitude for every admissible g, so it cuts toward the bullet conditionally.
events.remains: The bullet unconditionally.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 months; engagement not searched specifically
events.direction: Conditional on GRH; cuts toward infinitude for every admissible g under that hypothesis, with no counterexample.

events.what_happened: G. Cherubini and A. Perucca, 'On the vanishing of the density in Artin's conjecture on primitive roots', ORBilu preprint (deposited 22 May 2025 per the ORBilu record in search results; arXiv not found). Characterises when the Artin density over a number field is zero, building on Lenstra (1977). Over Q, density is nonzero except in the trivial cases, under GRH per the search summary. Not opened.
events.delivers: Characterisation of zero density for number fields, with the rational case conditional on GRH per the search summary. Not about infinitude for the integers.
events.remains: The bullet.
events.doubts: The date is an ORBilu deposit date, not a confirmed first public posting. Not opened.
events.direction: Analogue about the density; cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, arXiv:1707.06517, v14 (14 Feb 2026), retitled 'Simple Proof of the Primitive Root Conjecture' (comments: 'Seventeen Pages. Refined analysis of the error term.'). Abstract states: 'This note proves an unconditional asymptotic formula' for pi(u,x), the count of primes p <= x with u a primitive root, with a positive density constant delta(u) > 0, and says it strengthens Hooley's 1967 conditional result. v13 (15 Nov 2025) still claimed only the lower bound, so the asymptotic claim first appears here. Abstract page opened; body not read.
events.revisions: v13 15 Nov 2025 (lower bound only); v14 14 Feb 2026 (asymptotic; current in my fetch).
events.delivers: If correct: for each admissible u, an asymptotic count with positive density constant delta(u) > 0 for primes p <= x with u as primitive root, unconditionally. Implies infinitude for every admissible u, so it covers the bullet and goes beyond it to the density. The exact form of the error term and the density constant was not read.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet, if correct. The density is beyond what the bullet asks.
events.time_since_posted: 8 months to 11 Oct 2026; no review, journal decision or citing work found in my searches
events.doubts: The asymptotic claim is new in v14, after the lower-bound claim had been on arXiv since v8 in 2018 and unchanged through Nov 2025. The body was not read. Any unconditional asymptotic of Artin's form faces the same Hooley-type obstacle described for the 2018 claim (Persiflage, 8 Oct 2026, says Hooley's argument 'needs full GRH for these'). The Wikipedia article (as fetched) does not cite this paper.
events.direction: If correct, proves infinitude for every admissible u and the density form, cutting in the direction the conjecture points, with no counterexample.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'The quasi-Riemann hypothesis' (paper 003 in the release; path label 'October-5-2026', file paper2.pdf per the Wikipedia reference list). Not read. Per search summaries and Wikipedia, it claims a zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions: one catalogue entry says no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above 7/8. A companion gives Re(s) > 11/12 for the Riemann zeta function, which the README says was human-edited for readability. The sources disagree on these numbers. Per Wikipedia, the Artin proof is based on this manuscript. Scientific American reports that not all of the proofs were certified in Lean. Not refereed.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, preprint 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' (repository path label 'Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-integer-base-October-4-2026'; file primitive-roots-all-integer-bases.pdf). It is part of a release of 719 manuscripts in 372 families (722 in some reports), produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model and posted in the openai/math repository, whose only visible commit for this directory is dated 6 Oct 2026 ('Initial commit'). Per the VibeMathed entry, Theorem 1.1 states that for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square there are c_a > 0 and x_a such that for x >= x_a at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) have a as a primitive root. This gives infinitude for every such a, including a = 2, but not the predicted asymptotic. Wikipedia (as fetched) describes the paper as 'claiming an unconditional proof of the existence part'. Scientific American lists the Artin result among the release's results. Wikipedia and secondary reports say no mathematical community review has occurred. The PDF text could not be extracted, so the paper's own statement of hypotheses, disclosure and bibliography was not read.
events.revisions: The repository directory shows one visible commit, 'Initial commit', dated 6 Oct 2026. The README says 14 manuscripts received proof repairs and three were withdrawn for one sign error (withdrawn ones per secondary summaries: 'Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds', 'Algebraicity of Kuga-Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces', 'The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces'). This paper is not among the three; whether it is among the 14 repaired is not established. The date 4 Oct is the label on the preprint; the public posting I can document is 6 Oct.
events.delivers: If correct: infinitude of primes p with a as a primitive root, for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square, including a = 2 (lower bound c_a x/(log x)^2 for primes in (x, 2x)). Per VibeMathed, its proof is conditional on Theorem 1.2 (a zero-free strip for Hecke L-functions, which VibeMathed calls 'a very strong claim') and imports a Type II estimate from the companion Poisson-Dirichlet manuscript (Theorem 3.1) and mechanisms from the quasi-Riemann manuscript. The Lean statement (third-party formalization) is unconditional in form: for all a : Z with a != -1 and not a square, the set of primes p with orderOf (a mod p) = p - 1 is infinite. The Lean docstring for the main theorem says the result is unconditional.
events.remains: The predicted density (not asked by the bullet). For the bullet's infinitude, nothing remains if the claim is correct, but the claim depends on unrefereed companion results (Theorem 1.2, the Type II estimate, the quasi-Riemann mechanisms).

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (third-party formalization by Yao Xu, GitHub user cadamcat, repository artin-primitive-roots-lean4; not an OpenAI product)
machine_checked.note: Not resolved. In the files I could read: no 'sorry', 'admit', 'axiom' or 'native_decide' in Target.lean, Reduction.lean, Controlled.lean, Splitting.lean, or the theorem body of Hecke/Boundary.lean. But Hecke/Boundary.lean's header says the part-A theorem is 'sorry until the A chain is done' and its docstring says 'Sorry: this is what part A proves'; the body delegates to ArtinPrimitiveRoots.A2.thm_hecke_zero_free, which I did not read. Construction/Results.lean was read only in part (co_completion not seen). Splitting.lean's header says it is proved from thm:hecke-zero-free. The Hecke file's H1 and H2 hypotheses are not defined in the files I read. Verification/Axioms.lean runs #print axioms, but no output log is shown. The README says all proofs are verified by the Lean 4 kernel. VibeMathed (at its date) says 'No Lean main result'; Wikipedia (as fetched) says the Artin proof 'did not have a Lean formalization at the time of its release'.

events.doubts: (1) Conditionality is disputed. VibeMathed says the proof is conditional on Theorem 1.2 (a Hecke zero-free strip) and calls it 'a very strong claim'. The Wikipedia text (as fetched) and the Lean docstring say unconditional. Both can be true if Theorem 1.2 is proved in the same release, which the README implies, but then the claim stands or falls with that proof. (2) The chain depends on unrefereed companion manuscripts (the Poisson-Dirichlet Type II estimate, Theorem 3.1; the quasi-Riemann manuscript) and on the Hecke zero-free theorem, none of which I could read. (3) Persiflage (blog, 8 Oct 2026) reads the Artin argument as needing quasi-Riemann for Dedekind L-functions, which OpenAI reportedly proves only for Dirichlet L-functions. Its author calls this 'my first guess' and says the reconstruction is 'not at all surprising', and in a reply to a commenter writes that 'A closer look at Hooley's argument suggests that it needs full GRH for these'. This is a heuristic reading, not a check, but it names the gap. (4) The third-party Lean formalization shows the 'sorry until the A chain is done' comment in part A, and its imported modules were not all read. (5) The release has documented errors (three withdrawals for one sign error; the README warns that 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'); this paper is not in the Lean-verified part per VibeMathed. (6) No mathematician has publicly checked the argument in my sources; the 'reviews' are blog discussion, Scientific American's coverage, and a Zvi Mowshowitz roundup that says verification is pending.
events.direction: Proves the infinitude claim as stated, cutting in the direction the conjecture points, for every admissible a, including a = 2. It does not establish the predicted density.

events.what_happened: M. Ram Murty and Sunil Naik, 'A non-abelian large sieve and Artin's primitive root conjecture', arXiv:2608.21573 (v1, 21 Aug 2026). Abstract: 'Assuming the non-abelian large sieve inequality, we provide a proof of Artin's primitive root conjecture.' The abstract calls that inequality conjectured, and says the duality results are unconditional but only 'towards the conjectured non-abelian large sieve inequality'. The abstract excludes 'the integers 0, +-1 or a perfect square', which is the same class as the bullet's (neither a perfect square nor -1). Abstract page opened; body and introduction not read.

events.delivers: Conditional on the non-abelian large sieve inequality, which the abstract calls conjectured: infinitude of primes with a as a primitive root for every integer in the bullet's class. Unconditional content is only duality results toward the large sieve inequality, not about primitive roots directly.
events.remains: Unconditional infinitude for every admissible a, since the conditional input is unproved.

events.what_happened: Two manuscripts. (a) 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' claims that for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square there are c_a > 0 and x_a >= 2 such that, for every real x >= x_a, at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) satisfy p not dividing a and ord_p(a) = p - 1 (the main theorem of the introduction; the abstract states the same). The proof (01a-reduction.tex) builds primes p = c r Q + 1 with c in {2, 4}, Q > x^0.9 prime, and every prime factor of r in (exp((log x)^0.1), exp((log x)^0.3)), inside a residue class modulo M = 8 times the odd primes dividing a, chosen so that (a/p) = -1. This makes the index (p-1)/ord_p(a) odd. Primes whose index has Q as a factor are discarded using a bound on the product of |a^j - 1| for j up to 2x^0.1. Primes whose index has a prime factor l dividing r are discarded using a uniform Kummer-splitting bound (stated in 01a-reduction.tex, proved in 07-splitting.tex), which rests on the Hecke zero-free theorem (Theorem 1.2). (b) 'Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases' proves that for any finite set of distinct positive primes q_1, ..., q_k there are at least c x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) with p not dividing q_1...q_k and ord_p(q_i) = p - 1 for every i. It does this only under four stated Inputs (see conditional_on). Its k = 1 case is the Artin infinitude count restricted to positive prime bases.
events.delivers: For (a), the claim proves the infinitude assertion for every admissible base, and the statement matches the list's. The list asks, for each integer a that is not a square and not -1, whether a is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. The lower bound in (a) is positive in every sufficiently large dyadic interval, which gives infinitude. Restrictions: c_a and x_a depend on a, which the text states, and no uniformity in a is claimed. Negative bases other than -1 (for example -2, -3, -4) are covered by the signed squarefree decomposition a = d0 t^2 in the progression lemma, with the row d0 = -1 handling negative squares, and the Kummer bound is stated for |a| > 1. For (b), the claim gives infinitude only for positive prime bases, one or several at a time, and only conditionally on the four Inputs. It adds no unconditional case beyond (a) and does not cover composite or negative bases.
events.remains: If (a) is correct, the infinitude statement of the bullet is fully covered and nothing in it remains open. Not established by either manuscript: the predicted order x/log x (the manuscripts prove x/(log x)^2 only), the asymptotic density with Artin's constant mentioned in the Wikipedia lead (outside the bullet), and any uniformity of c_a and x_a in a. For (b), the unconditional simultaneous case remains open, and so do all bases that are not positive primes.
events.doubts: (a) The analytic core, Theorem 1.2, has no conductor or height cutoff and one width, 10^-6, for all cyclotomic fields containing mu_12 and all finite-order Hecke characters; the text says 'the width is common to all fields and characters in the statement'. The introduction describes the standard simultaneous zero-free regions as having logarithmic width and permitting at most one simple real exceptional zero (citing Thorner-Zaman, Theorem 3.1), and presents the common width as the new step. The text does not compare it with a published result of this strength. Cyclotomic Dedekind zeta functions factor into Dirichlet L-functions, so the statement as written also covers every Dirichlet L-function. The text does not discuss that consequence. The Hecke argument is described as built 'over each fixed F' from mechanisms of the companion 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis', which the introduction says treats Q(sqrt(-3)). The marked Type II estimate is imported from the Poisson-Dirichlet companion; the coefficient criterion's dependence is 'extracted' from that argument, and the introduction says the authors verify the character and frequency estimates themselves. (b) The four Inputs are hypotheses, and the text says their proofs lie in (a) and its companions, so (b) inherits the doubts in (a). The abstract's first sentence states the result without the condition, which appears only in its last sentence. The introduction counts four Inputs, but Input 2 has two parts, so there are five displayed hypotheses. Coverage: I did not read sections 02-06, the proof of Theorem 1.2, the fixed-progression construction in 12-construction.tex, or the appendix in full. A keyword search of those sections found no 'sketch' or 'left to the reader' style flags. The points above rest on the introduction, the reduction, the rough-Type II and sieve statements I read, and the Inputs of (b).; conditional on: (a) assumes no hypothesis of its own, but depends on work outside its text: (i) 'The Poisson-Dirichlet law for the prime factors of p-1', Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 5.2, for the one-sided marked Type II estimate; the text says its coefficient criterion (Lemma 10.2) extracts the coefficient dependence from that companion's argument. (ii) 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis', Part I, Sections 5-7, whose coefficient reflection and additive probe the text adapts over each cyclotomic field. (iii) Dunn and Radziwill, Section 5.1 and Appendix A, for theta comparison formulas. (iv) Kazhdan and Patterson's cubic theta representation with their erratum, and Patterson's cubic theta series, for the normalization. (v) The block-sieve and rough-density forms, adapted from 'BlockPaper' (Lemmas 2.9 and 7.4), with proofs included in the text. (b) assumes four Inputs, which it attributes to (a): the uniform Hecke zero-free assertion (the same as (a)'s Theorem 1.2: no zeros of L_F(s, eta) for Re s > 1 - 10^-6, for every finite-order Hecke character of a cyclotomic field containing mu_12); the marked Type II estimate in two parts, (i) the coefficient criterion (= (a)'s Lemma 10.2) and (ii) rough-factor cancellation (= (a)'s Proposition 10.3); the block sieve (= (a)'s Lemma 11.1); and the rough-number density (= (a)'s Lemma 11.2). Its splitting proof also takes the abelian tower argument and the prime-ideal count from (a)'s Section 9, equations (9.2) and (9.5)-(9.9), as cited.
events.direction: proves the infinitude assertion for every admissible base (a); conditional proof of infinitude for positive prime bases, simultaneously (b)

summary: As of 26 January 2024 the bullet was open, with infinitude known only under GRH (Hooley 1967) and unconditionally for at most two exceptional a plus the three-candidate result of Heath-Brown (1986); no unconditional result covers any specific integer. The September-October 2026 window contains one major event. OpenAI's openai/math repository, in a release produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, includes a preprint 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' (path-dated 4 Oct 2026; repository commit 6 Oct 2026). Per the VibeMathed entry's reading of Theorem 1.1, it gives at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in (x,2x) with a as a primitive root for every a that is neither -1 nor a square, including a = 2. That is the bullet's infinitude claim. Whether it is unconditional is disputed by my sources. The Wikipedia text (as fetched) and the third-party Lean theorem and docstring describe it as unconditional. VibeMathed says the proof is conditional on Theorem 1.2, a Hecke zero-free strip it calls very strong, and imports a Type II estimate from a companion manuscript (Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors, Theorem 3.1), plus mechanisms from a quasi-Riemann manuscript; all are unrefereed and in the same release. The third-party Lean 4 formalization (cadamcat/artin-primitive-roots-lean4) shows no sorry in the theorem file or in the reduction, controlled and splitting files I could read, but its Hecke/Boundary.lean header says the part-A theorem is 'sorry until the A chain is done' and its body delegates to modules I could not read; the formal chain's sorry status is unresolved, and no build log is visible. The only AI attribution is the release README's statement that 'the vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model'. The Artin paper's own disclosure could not be read because the repository PDF did not extract, so that README sentence is the lab's account rather than the authors' sentence about this paper. I found no human check of the OpenAI argument. The Persiflage blog (6 and 8 Oct 2026) reads the strategy and says the author has not verified it ('gut feeling', 'my first guess'). Scientific American and the Zvi roundup report that verification is pending. Separately, N. A. Carella's arXiv:1707.06517 has claimed infinitude since 17 Nov 2018 (v8; base-10 only in v1-v7 from July 2017), with an abstract that states no GRH; v14 (14 Feb 2026) first claims an unconditional asymptotic. No engagement was found for any version. Murty and Naik (21 Aug 2026) prove infinitude conditional on a conjectured non-abelian large sieve inequality. The remaining events are conditional (GRH: Hooley 1967, Perucca-Shparlinski Jan 2024 before the frozen revision, Kimmel 2023, Fan-Pollack 2025, Goldmakher-Martin-Peringuey 2025 with unspecified weaker unconditional statements) or partial (Klurman-Shparlinski-Teravainen, BLMS 2025, almost all a in a growing range, which gives no specific a). Neighbouring results are analogues or different questions: function fields (Hochfilzer-Waxman 2023), two-variable Artin (Hazra-Murty-Sivaraman 2024), density vanishing (Cherubini-Perucca 2025), and Naik's unconditional Matsuda-monoid result (Oct 2024), which uses Artin's conjecture without, as far as the abstract shows, proving it. The Erdos #985 forum thread mentions a GPT-5.4 Thinking literature search, but it concerns primes q < p that are primitive roots mod p, not this bullet. No refereed proof of the bullet for every admissible a was found. Where a call was close, both readings are in the events: the OpenAI claim could count as an unconditional AI-attributed proof of infinitude that is unrefereed, or as a conditional one whose inputs are unrefereed and whose formal chain is incomplete.
competing_reading: Read the OpenAI preprint as a proof of the bullet. The bullet asks only for infinitude; the claimed lower bound gives it directly for every admissible a, including 2; the Lean theorem statement matches the bullet's class; the lab's README and the Lean docstring say the result is unconditional; and the author is a model with no human author named. On that reading it is an unrefereed, AI-attributed proof that would settle the bullet if it holds. The opposing reading: the same authors' argument rests on companion results in the same release (a Hecke zero-free theorem, a Type II estimate, quasi-Riemann mechanisms), which VibeMathed calls conditional and which are unrefereed; the Lean chain has a documented sorry in part A; and the blog reading suggests the Hooley-type argument needs full GRH. On that reading, 'unconditional' holds only at the level of the lab's claim, and the bullet is not resolved until those inputs are checked. The Carella claim is a third reading: an unrefereed general claim available since 2018 that has drawn no engagement, which the judging pass may or may not count.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The OpenAI preprint's full text (TeX source or a readable PDF): its own statement of hypotheses, whether Theorems 1.2 and 3.1 are proved within the same paper, its disclosure of AI use, and its bibliography. (2) A Lean build log for cadamcat/artin-primitive-roots-lean4 with the #print axioms output for artin_primitive_roots_infinite, and confirmation that the A2.Endpoint, Construction and Hecke/Continuation modules contain no sorryAx. (3) Expert reports or a referee decision on the Type II estimate (Poisson-Dirichlet manuscript) and the Hecke zero-free theorem. (4) The openai/math correction history for this manuscript, showing whether it was repaired or withdrawn, and the CONTENTS.md entry for it. (5) For Carella: the body of v14, and any journal submission or expert response; the body of v8 for how it avoids the Hooley barrier. (6) For Murty-Naik: the introduction, to see how the non-abelian large sieve is stated and whether it is a known conjecture.

event.what_happened: OpenAI, preprint 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' (repository path label 'Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-integer-base-October-4-2026'; file primitive-roots-all-integer-bases.pdf). It is part of a release of 719 manuscripts in 372 families (722 in some reports), produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model and posted in the openai/math repository, whose only visible commit for this directory is dated 6 Oct 2026 ('Initial commit'). Per the VibeMathed entry, Theorem 1.1 states that for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square there are c_a > 0 and x_a such that for x >= x_a at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) have a as a primitive root. This gives infinitude for every such a, including a = 2, but not the predicted asymptotic. Wikipedia (as fetched) describes the paper as 'claiming an unconditional proof of the existence part'. Scientific American lists the Artin result among the release's results. Wikipedia and secondary reports say no mathematical community review has occurred. The PDF text could not be extracted, so the paper's own statement of hypotheses, disclosure and bibliography was not read.
event.revisions: The repository directory shows one visible commit, 'Initial commit', dated 6 Oct 2026. The README says 14 manuscripts received proof repairs and three were withdrawn for one sign error (withdrawn ones per secondary summaries: 'Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds', 'Algebraicity of Kuga-Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces', 'The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces'). This paper is not among the three; whether it is among the 14 repaired is not established. The date 4 Oct is the label on the preprint; the public posting I can document is 6 Oct.
event.delivers: If correct: infinitude of primes p with a as a primitive root, for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square, including a = 2 (lower bound c_a x/(log x)^2 for primes in (x, 2x)). Per VibeMathed, its proof is conditional on Theorem 1.2 (a zero-free strip for Hecke L-functions, which VibeMathed calls 'a very strong claim') and imports a Type II estimate from the companion Poisson-Dirichlet manuscript (Theorem 3.1) and mechanisms from the quasi-Riemann manuscript. The Lean statement (third-party formalization) is unconditional in form: for all a : Z with a != -1 and not a square, the set of primes p with orderOf (a mod p) = p - 1 is infinite. The Lean docstring for the main theorem says the result is unconditional.
event.remains: The predicted density (not asked by the bullet). For the bullet's infinitude, nothing remains if the claim is correct, but the claim depends on unrefereed companion results (Theorem 1.2, the Type II estimate, the quasi-Riemann mechanisms).

machine_checked.note: Not resolved. In the files I could read: no 'sorry', 'admit', 'axiom' or 'native_decide' in Target.lean, Reduction.lean, Controlled.lean, Splitting.lean, or the theorem body of Hecke/Boundary.lean. But Hecke/Boundary.lean's header says the part-A theorem is 'sorry until the A chain is done' and its docstring says 'Sorry: this is what part A proves'; the body delegates to ArtinPrimitiveRoots.A2.thm_hecke_zero_free, which I did not read. Construction/Results.lean was read only in part (co_completion not seen). Splitting.lean's header says it is proved from thm:hecke-zero-free. The Hecke file's H1 and H2 hypotheses are not defined in the files I read. Verification/Axioms.lean runs #print axioms, but no output log is shown. The README says all proofs are verified by the Lean 4 kernel. VibeMathed (at its date) says 'No Lean main result'; Wikipedia (as fetched) says the Artin proof 'did not have a Lean formalization at the time of its release'.

event.doubts: (1) Conditionality is disputed. VibeMathed says the proof is conditional on Theorem 1.2 (a Hecke zero-free strip) and calls it 'a very strong claim'. The Wikipedia text (as fetched) and the Lean docstring say unconditional. Both can be true if Theorem 1.2 is proved in the same release, which the README implies, but then the claim stands or falls with that proof. (2) The chain depends on unrefereed companion manuscripts (the Poisson-Dirichlet Type II estimate, Theorem 3.1; the quasi-Riemann manuscript) and on the Hecke zero-free theorem, none of which I could read. (3) Persiflage (blog, 8 Oct 2026) reads the Artin argument as needing quasi-Riemann for Dedekind L-functions, which OpenAI reportedly proves only for Dirichlet L-functions. Its author calls this 'my first guess' and says the reconstruction is 'not at all surprising', and in a reply to a commenter writes that 'A closer look at Hooley's argument suggests that it needs full GRH for these'. This is a heuristic reading, not a check, but it names the gap. (4) The third-party Lean formalization shows the 'sorry until the A chain is done' comment in part A, and its imported modules were not all read. (5) The release has documented errors (three withdrawals for one sign error; the README warns that 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'); this paper is not in the Lean-verified part per VibeMathed. (6) No mathematician has publicly checked the argument in my sources; the 'reviews' are blog discussion, Scientific American's coverage, and a Zvi Mowshowitz roundup that says verification is pending.
event.direction: Proves the infinitude claim as stated, cutting in the direction the conjecture points, for every admissible a, including a = 2. It does not establish the predicted density.

judgement.why: The statement asks only for infinitude for every admissible a, so the OpenAI theorem (c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in (x,2x) for every non-square a != -1) is whole in scope; it is unreviewed (VibeMathed is a catalogue, Persiflage explicitly did not verify, Lean chain has a sorry) and doubtful rather than not_credible because it is days old and the doubt is specific but not an identified error: its Theorem 1.2 would give a uniform zero-free strip for all Dirichlet L-functions, a result far beyond known technology. AI role is generated from the lab README with no human author. GRH- or conjecture-conditional results (Hooley, Fan-Pollack, Goldmakher et al., Perucca-Shparlinski, Murty-Naik) are reductions to unproved hypotheses and score none; average-over-a, function-field, number-field, two-variable and monoid results are variants. Heath-Brown's 'all but at most two a' is a case. Carella's claims score whole/case but not_credible on multiple F10 signals (eight years of silence on a landmark claim, scope ballooning across 14 revisions, later work still calling it open, no answer to the GRH barrier). The two companion manuscripts are an input lemma (none) and a zero-free-region result for a different question (variant).
judgement.doubts: openai-math-029 and openai-2026-10-primitive-roots-all-bases describe the same manuscript (029 also bundles the conditional simultaneous-bases paper); they are answered identically. The record does not confirm the README's 'vast majority' sentence covers this specific manuscript, though no human author is named and it is not among the named exceptions. Carella's progressions paper is unclear on whether q = 1 is included; judged whole but set aside as not_credible either way. Gupta-Murty could be read as a case; judged none since it settles no specific a.
